claims.text: The starting catalyst is a near-equiatomic, multi-element automotive alloy containing platinum-group metals and base metals.
The as-synthesized catalyst has dispersed active material.
An ultrathin CeO2 overlayer can be deposited on the catalyst by ALD at approximately 200°C with controlled thickness.
The deposited CeO2 layer will be conformal and highly dispersed.
The CeO2 overlayer will form an intimate interface with the alloy catalyst surface.
CeO2 provides oxygen-storage and redox behavior capable of buffering exhaust-environment fluctuations.
Redox buffering by the CeO2 overlayer will mitigate sintering of active platinum-group-metal sites during thermal cycling and H2O/NO exposure.
The CeO2 overlayer will mitigate phase segregation during thermal cycling and H2O/NO exposure.
Suppressing sintering and phase segregation will stabilize the dispersion and accessibility of active platinum-group-metal sites.
An optimized ultrathin CeO2 layer can protect the catalyst without materially blocking active sites.
A CeO2 overlayer ideally below 1 nm will improve low-temperature catalytic conversion relative to the untreated catalyst.
The CeO2-coated catalyst will retain activity better during prolonged transient operation and accelerated thermal aging than the untreated catalyst.
Applying the CeO2 overlayer will maintain low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The untreated catalyst is prone to sintering under transient, low-temperature, chemically reactive exhaust conditions.
The untreated catalyst is prone to phase segregation and deactivation under transient, low-temperature, chemically reactive exhaust conditions.
CeO2 layers thicker than the ultrathin target range could block catalytic active sites.
The proposed benefit is limited to a thickness window near or below 1 nm and to gasoline or hybrid exhaust containing H2O and NO at low operating temperatures.
